content.text: Missing invariant that v is the minimum of the prefix; the bridge to the first postcondition fails.

input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "bridge",
 "diagnosis": "The loop invariants only say v equals the length of some list in s[..i]; they never state that v is <= the length of every list processed so far. After the loop Dafny knows only the invariants and i == |s|, so the postcondition 'forall i :: 0 <= i < |s| ==> v <= |s[i]|' cannot be derived. Adding the invariant 'forall k :: 0 <= k < i ==> v <= |s[k]|' bridges the loop to the postcondition."}
EOF
sed -i '9a\        invariant forall k :: 0 <= k < i ==> v <= |s[k]|' program.dfy
dafny verify program.dfy

content.content: Dafny program verifier finished with 2 verified, 0 errors

tool_use_result.stdout: Dafny program verifier finished with 2 verified, 0 errors

content.text:
Fixed: `program.dfy` now verifies (`2 verified, 0 errors`).

**What was wrong:** The loop invariants only said that `v` equals the length of some list in `s[..i]`. Nothing said `v` was no larger than every list length seen so far. After the loop, Dafny only knows the invariants plus `i == |s|`, so it couldn't prove the first `ensures` clause (`v <= |s[i]|` for every `i`). This is a gap in the loop invariant at the step from loop exit to the postcondition (the "bridge" step).

**The fix:** I added this invariant at line 10:
```dafny
invariant forall k :: 0 <= k < i ==> v <= |s[k]|
```
It holds on entry, because `i == 1` and `v == |s[0]|`. The loop body keeps it true, because `v` only drops to `|s[i]|` when that length is smaller. At exit, with `i == |s|`, it gives the postcondition directly. Nothing else in the file changed. I wrote `diagnosis.json` before the edit, classifying the problem as invariant / bridge.
